verdict: Uber's bookings grew 25% to $53.7B and operating profit rose 57% to $1.9B — but a $1.5B paper loss on its investment stakes cut reported profit to $282M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: cut by a $1.5B paper loss on investments

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Bookings rose 25%, but revenue grew just 5%: business-model changes in how some trips are billed (insurance and driver costs) reshape the top line.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers, growing far faster than rides.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Running the platform day to day — support, operations and local teams.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Promotions, advertising and winning riders, eaters and drivers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its autonomous-vehicle partnerships.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and the back office.

follow100Note: Of the $2.14 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $0.14 belongs to non-controlling partners — $1.99 is Uber shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Bookings still booming
takeaways.text: Gross Bookings — everything riders and eaters spent on the platform — grew 25% to $53.7B, with trips up 20% to 3.6 billion and 50 million Uber One members. Revenue grew 14% to $13.2B; billing-model changes held reported Mobility revenue growth to 5% even as ride bookings rose 25%.

takeaways.title: Core profit up 57%
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 57% to $1.9B and Adjusted EBITDA 33% to $2.5B. The cleaner read on this quarter is the operating line — the bottom line was decided by investments, not by rides or deliveries.

takeaways.title: A paper loss did the damage
takeaways.text: Other expense, net, was $1,494M — mostly a $1,474M unrealized loss on debt and equity securities. It cut reported net income to $282M ($263M to Uber shareholders, $0.13 a share), down from $1,774M a year ago, when a tax benefit flattered results instead.

oneTimers: An unrealized loss of about $1,474M on debt and equity securities sits in other income (expense), net — a paper loss on the value of Uber's investment stakes, not cash lost from rides or deliveries.
otherDetail: Interest income of $175M, less $108M of interest expense, a $1,494M other-expense line — mostly a $1,474M unrealized loss on debt and equity securities — and a $20M equity-method loss.
footerNote: Net income of $282M includes $19M attributable to non-controlling interests; $263M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.13 EPS figure). Cost of revenue is shown excluding depreciation and amortization, exactly as Uber reports it.
